ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the curve in the figure is labeled f'', representing the second derivative of the function f. The curve is tangent to the x-axis at x=a, only touching the x-axis and then still remaining below the x-axis; at x=d it passes through the x-axis, changing from negative values to positive values. The figure also marks b and c, but they are not zeros of f''. Then reason: the inflection points of the function f occur at positions where f'' changes sign. Since f'' is negative on both sides of a, there is no sign change, so x=a is not an inflection point. Since f'' changes from negative to positive at d, a sign change occurs, so f has an inflection point at x=d.
